messages:
maya: Heads up — upstream advisory for CVE-2026-2147 in kms-connector (v1.4.2). Patch available v1.4.3. Affects our kms client used by Dedicated + Private. Exploit path requires a local agent with cache enabled, but could expose plaintext key material from the agent KV cache. marking P2/P1 depending on customer tier :warning:
kevin: link to advisory: https://oss-vuln.example.com/CVE-2026-2147 — exploitability: low remote, higher if attacker has local access. patch notes say: 'fix cache deserialization bug that allowed forging of cache entries'
tyler: SLA impact question — will this require downtime for Dedicated? any per-region concerns?
rachel-oncall: quick scan done: security-bot reports 12 Dedicated hosts and 3 Private images still pinned at 1.4.2. Hosted-runtime uses managed image with patched runtime (already on 1.4.3 in canary). So Hosted risk is near-zero. Dedicated — surface area is customers using our KMS proxy (mostly enterprise).
security-bot: automated-scan: affected: 12 dedicated nodes, 3 private images. exploit-confidence: medium. recommended-action: schedule patch and canary.
maya: Key considerations: 1) HSM/KMS integrations call native libs that we must test — libsec upgrade in v1.4.3 changes rotation handshake timing. 2) Some Private customers build custom agent images; we can't auto-push there. 3) There's a config flag `kms.cache.enable_legacy_deser` that can be toggled to mitigate without upgrading (disables legacy path).
kevin: Proposed plan: - immediate mitigation: flip `kms.cache.enable_legacy_deser=false` for Dedicated pools (no restart). - schedule binary upgrade to 1.4.3 in a 2-stage rollout: canary (2 nodes) -> regional -> global. Run HSM/rotation test suite after canary.
eti-sre: fwiw, set flag via feature-flags will take effect within 90s, low risk. I can push flag to prod/dedicated-canary now.
tyler: customer comms: enterprise customers (SLA-paying) should be informed pre-rollout. Non-enterprise Dedicated might be rolled silently but still notify post-change. Private: notify and offer assisted upgrade; assume opt-in.
maya: timeline suggestion: canary tonight 22:00 UTC (minimal traffic), monitor 24h, if clean then regional rollouts starting tomorrow morning. If tests of HSM rotation fail, fallback to toggle-only mitigation and notify customers.
eli-sre: need to confirm maintenance windows for EMEA dedicated clusters — Ops calendar says EMEA window is 02:00-04:00 local; can we align?
rachel-oncall: Ops: canary tonight 22:00 UTC for us is 23:00 EMEA — slightly outside window but acceptable for 2-node canary. Full rollout should target each region's maintenance window.
kevin: Risk matrix: - Hosted: patched (canary) — low risk. - Dedicated (enterprise): medium risk due to HSM timing changes — require testing + customer notice. - Dedicated (self-serve): low-medium; can roll silently but monitor. - Private: high-process overhead (opt-in) — we should prepare a changelog + upgrade guide.
maya: Testing checklist for canary: - run E2E key rotation against SoftHSM + NitroHSM, - run perf smoke (latency, 99th), - validate audit log entries unchanged, - verify no key export paths exposed.
tyler: I'll draft a short customer bulletin for enterprise customers: what happened, mitigation steps, proposed rollout times, and support contact.
kevin: one more mitigation idea: add temporary ACL rule to KMS proxy to restrict agent debug endpoints for dedicated clusters. Low risk and buys time.
maya: decision: flip legacy deser flag now for Dedicated pools (eli, rachel please). Schedule canary upgrade to kms-connector 1.4.3 tonight 22:00 UTC on 2 nodes in dedicated-canary. Monitor 24h; if green start regional rollouts aligned to maintenance windows. Private: notify customers with upgrade playbook and offer assisted upgrade.
eli-sre: flipping flag now. patch plan ticket: INFSEC-3412 (canary at 22:00 UTC).
rachel-oncall: I'll coordinate monitoring dashboards and oncall rotation for the window. I'll also post to #status if we need a broader notice. :thumbsup:
kevin: logging note — add synthetic check to ensure audit logs still contain rotation events after patch.
maya: thanks all — will update incident doc and paste final plan into ticket. If anything else pops up ping me directly. :lock:
